key_insight: AI-guided single-cell imaging and label-free enrichment revealed morphological heterogeneity and shared and divergent genomic alterations in metastatic breast cancer effusions.
clinical_relevance: Malignant effusions may offer an accessible source for studying metastatic tumor diversity, although clinical utility remains unproven.
method: Applied a pretrained deep-learning model to single-cell brightfield images to estimate tumor fractions and characterize morphology.
Used morphology-guided microfluidics to enrich tumor cells without labels.
Profiled enriched-cell genomes and compared them with available matched effusion cell-free DNA and solid tumors.
evidence_signal: In 10 patients, imaging identified putative tumor cells in 25 samples (median tumor fraction, 5.4%); immune-cell estimates correlated with flow cytometry (r = 0.69–0.75), and genomic profiling supported tumor origin and relatedness.
watch_item: The small cohort and tumor-fraction-dependent genomic signal warrant broader validation before clinical implementation.
paper_title: AI-powered single-cell imaging and morphology-guided label-free enrichment reveal tumor heterogeneity, genomic relatedness, and divergence in malignant effusions
